candidate.blueprint_locator: Psychosocial Integrity: assess client coping and emotional responses to illness/treatment, use therapeutic communication, and facilitate support systems/resources.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Psychosocial Integrity — coping with chronic dialysis, role disruption, and referral for support
candidate.educational_objective: Assess psychosocial coping when dialysis disrupts work, roles, and activities and connect the client with renal social-work or mental-health resources when support is needed.

options.A: Explain that these disruptions are unavoidable and redirect the discussion to the dialysis prescription.
options.B: Advise the client to stop working until adapting emotionally to dialysis.
options.C: Assess the client's coping and emotional concerns and offer referral to the dialysis social worker or mental health support.
options.D: Reassure the client that most people stop feeling overwhelmed after several months of dialysis.

candidate.rationale: NIDDK notes that in-center hemodialysis can require changes in work, home life, activities, and responsibilities and that adjusting to kidney failure and time spent on dialysis can be difficult. It specifically identifies a mental health counselor or social worker as resources to help clients cope. C therefore addresses the client's expressed psychosocial burden with assessment and appropriate support. A minimizes the concern, B makes an unnecessary employment decision for the client, and D gives unsupported reassurance and imposes a fixed adjustment timeline.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Dialysis can substantially disrupt roles and daily life, and clients experiencing psychosocial difficulty should have coping concerns assessed and may benefit from social-work or mental-health support.
candidate.source_locator: Hemodialysis > What changes will I have to make when I start hemodialysis?: dialysis requires routine adjustment; work/home life, activities, and responsibilities may change; accepting changes can be hard; a mental health counselor or social worker can help with coping. What Is Kidney Failure? > How will kidney failure affect how I feel about my life?: coping can be stressful; depression can occur with chronic illness; health care team and support resources can help.
candidate.source_organization: National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases (NIDDK), NIH
candidate.stem: A client receiving long-term in-center hemodialysis says, 'Treatment is taking over my life. I am missing work, giving up activities, and I feel overwhelmed.' Which nursing action is best?
